title: Anti AI horde getting at you in the comments under your post? I’ll back you up! (+bonus tip on music generation)
author: New_Complaint5282
selftext:
I’ve posted about my game yesterday, got some anti AI deep thinkers traffic there. At first I decided to just ignore it, but… I just couldn’t help myself and started “discussing” with them.     
Because this is so annoying. You spend countless hours on something. The newest tech gives you opportunities you always dreamt of. You are very excited. And then this guy comes. Spends 3 seconds looking at your post. And he writes:

Slop

Oh my… 

So I started answering. This is obviously a waste of my time and energy, but im in that kind of mood right now 🤣    
Anyway, I realised I’m being attacked by a horde, but I’m the only one on my side.     
So I thought I’d do something good today. If you’re in a similar situation, let me know, I’ll drop some comments in your post. But only if your project has the quality - if you spam the slop, you’re on your own 😁

Now the bonus because, you know… the rules.   
I’m pretty happy about how the music in my game ended up, so I can share a few tips on that:  
1. Use Gemini. It’s cheap, and it can do a very decent job.  
2. If you want amazing music - buy it though.   
3. Use instrumental mode.   
4. Work hard on your base prompt for tracks. Adjust it, generate more. Settle only when you get a few consistent and satisfying results out of the same prompt.   
5. When you have it, you can adjust it for different tracks.   
6. Always generate at least 3 tracks for 1 desired. Choose best.   
7. 10-20% of tracks will be broken (cut beats, sounding really off etc)  
8. I have seen no difference in quality or consistency between keeping a session long and generating one track per session.

replies.author: bot_exe
replies.body:
I don't understand how that relates to my comment. I make music and it's meaningful for a series of reasons. I have used AI, among many other tools, in assisting me as well. I have also heard a lot of AI slop music and human slop music as well, the AI isn't really the issue.

But my original point was answering your question "how does one make ai assisted music with ai without generating the whole thing?" Well you do it by using AI to assist you without generating the whole thing. Like I mentioned you can use it to generate midi, or make samples or help you build an instrument or to learn music theory or make a chord progression or learn a new synthesis/sampling/playing technique or synthesize speech to sample... I meant the possibilities are kind of endless with modern AI. I have done all that and probably I'm just scratching the surface of what is possible.

And showing that "the only reason programming has any kind of nuance to it is because you can use ai in different ways without generating the whole thing."

Is also true of other mediums beyond coding if you care enough to use it in a nuanced way.

>"its hard for me to see how you could possibly ever need ai for music."  

It's not really "a need", it's just very useful and nice to work with for some things.

I just finished building an expanded version of this[ instrument](https://youtube.com/shorts/LPbQgl6Dv0Q?si=KnPhbPv1wWm2qmdE). Claude helped me figure out the math for some of the more complicated parts. I kept expanding on it and it got quite complex, so then I made it write a whole document so I don't forget later how it works (which is what tends to happen when I have to take long breaks from this hobby to do life's responsibilities). This is just one way in which can you use AI to help you produce music without making slop.

I get the anti Ai stuff honestly.  
Im an artist, i know how to do all teh things, game design, animation, 3d, music, hell man i can do hand drawn cell animation and paint lol. 

what I cant do is afford a programmer to make the things I want to make. thats what people dont realize, AI lets you do things YOU want to do not what some money dude is willing to pay for you to make.  its like giving us artists the tool to really make that dream project we always wanted to make.

the people who say slop don't understand how frustrating it is in the industry just trying to get something made if you dont have the money.  artists, programmers, musicians and voice artists are hard to come by.  no one wants to work for free and i for one don't blame them.

I think all of us would pay a programmer, artist or whoever if we could.

so people who say slop just don't understand where most of us are comming from or what it takes to actually get a game made.

that said, if you can actually make content for your game imo, you should. thats why Ido the art for my projects instead of generating stuff.
